chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the one in Ihram who killed a locust. He said: 'A handful of food; and if there were many, so upon him is the blood of a sheep.'

key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: Blood of a sheep (a specific type of fidya)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a locust while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the fidya for killing a single locust is specified as a handful of food, reflecting the principle of proportional expiation for minor game. The text further clarifies that if the quantity is significant, the penalty escalates to the blood of a sheep, demonstrating the juristic distinction between negligible and substantial loss of game while in Ihram. This ruling underscores the meticulous attention to detail in Shia fiqh regarding the sanctity of the sacred state.
